title: Test actual older Git for Windows source-reader fallback
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Complete the actual older-Git-for-Windows handoff in [Discussion #4681](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/4681#discussioncomment-19152845). Official MinGit **2.35.3.windows.1** really rejects `git cat-file --batch -z` with exit 129 and no stdout; the unchanged source reader falls back once and returns the exact objects. Git **2.47.1.windows.1** is the supported-protocol control.

Add four installed-Git tests and a [source-pinned evidence/reproduction note](https://github.com/mihir-s-05/integer-mult-bounds/blob/0f184845dca823c5cb3fe3f13ef61fe977716d08/docs/research/windows-installed-git.md). Git object trees represent literal LF/CR/CRLF names without creating forbidden Windows filenames. Coverage includes independent SHA-1/SHA-256 blob IDs, empty/large binary/Unicode payloads, duplicate reads, early closure, invalid requests, actual process/pipe cleanup and watchdog removal. The observer retains the real executable, arguments and pipes; on the unsupported binary, exact-byte tests wait for its real rejection before returning the handle to exercise closed stdin.

This is tooling compatibility evidence. Production code, frozen inputs and the selected frontier are unchanged.

## Task and overlap

- Canonical main base: `7c472563474e60185e6ca101a17622133d047e56`, unchanged on submission refresh; priority revision 7.
- Contribution head: `0f184845dca823c5cb3fe3f13ef61fe977716d08`.
- Task `portable-replay`, scope **changed** from canonical-payload comparison to the explicit installed-Git source-transport handoff: source pins must be readable before independent replay.
- Complements #2752's compatibility controls, #4686's Windows closed-pipe repair, and #4738/#5185's deadline/ownership work already present in this base. This adds an actual old Windows executable and portable object-only fixtures, not another simulated option rejection.
- Refreshed overlap: 305 open PR bodies and 4,637 Discussion records, complete remote pagination at 19:13 UTC; local sparse-note coverage remains incomplete.

## Validation

Windows 11 build 26300, CPython 3.12.0 x64, `PYTHONUTF8=1`; MinGit archive verified against the publisher's SHA256.

```sh
python -W error -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_git_*.py' -v
python -O -W error -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_git_*.py' -v
```

For **each Windows Git version and each Python mode**: 61 discovered, **53 passed and 8 skipped**. The skips are six existing POSIX descendant tests and two existing physical CR/LF filename fixtures; all four new tests run on Windows. The old full suite preceded final failure-only test teardown cleanup; the final new module was rerun successfully normally and with `-O`. On WSL Ubuntu, Git 2.43.0 / Python 3.12.3, the final new module also passes all four tests in both modes.

Two disposable source mutations—disable fallback, or bypass literal CR/LF resolution—each make the new exact-object test fail. `git diff --cached --check` passed. Exact commands, timings, binary/source hashes and limitations are in the note.

The initial default-encoding broader Windows run had an existing Unicode diagnostic-spelling assertion failure; rejection still occurred. It is documented, not counted as a pass or fixed here. Direct-child stall tests use controlled Python subprocesses; native Windows descendant-held pipes are unverified. No selected cold replay, mathematical/proof-kernel verification or hosted-CI success is claimed by this local evidence.

## Credit

Retain Nick Petalas (#2752), Mihir Srivastava (#4686), Brian / JoyboyBrian (#4738/#5185), Woklerx, Arham Tahir and Douglas Colkitt's reader/source-contract credit, and Tekalign's object-tree fixture lineage. Prepared for Mihir Srivastava with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, one agent. Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

The evidence note leaves two separate, unclaimed follow-ups: a native Windows descendant-held-pipe ownership fixture (first prove readiness and survival after leader exit), and the existing Windows diagnostic-encoding assertion. Neither blocks this version-pair compatibility result.
